clue.text: Police officer, depressed, needs confidence

parts.note: feeling depressed is feeling blue
bottle is British slang for nerve or confidence

explanation.surface: A gloomy policeman needs a boost of self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE is British slang for courage. 'needs' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is old British slang for a uniformed constable, from the blue of the uniform.

clue.text: Sailor appearing in live film

indicators.note: the sailor shows up inside the word for live, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman turns up in a film shot live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is the definition, not part of the wordplay: the piglet movie. 'appearing in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe is the 1995 family movie about a sheep-herding piglet.

clue.text: Continually holds up a group of soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the held letters are read from the bottom upwards
the long word holds a short run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps propping up an army squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' points to TINU inside contINUally; 'up' turns it, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a military formation such as a company or battalion.

clue.text: Radio transmitter's range in English town

parts.note: a beacon is a signalling transmitter; the possessive adds an S
a field is a range or area, as in field of vision

explanation.surface: How far a radio signal reaches somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: BEACONSFIELD is a market town in Buckinghamshire, west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a town in the English home counties, in Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: Giant bird circling North America

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: going round turns the abbreviation the other way about

explanation.surface: An enormous bird flies round the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' turns the North America abbreviation round, giving AN after the bird; 'Giant' reads as an adjective for the bird but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant elder gods of Greek myth, so any colossus is so named.

clue.text: City dwellers not quite accepted among antisocial types

indicators.note: the trimmed word sits among the letters of the antisocial types

parts.note: loners are people who shun company

indicators.note: not quite complete, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the done thing is the accepted thing

explanation.surface: Townsfolk who are not fully welcomed by a crowd of recluses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of the accepted thing, giving DON; 'among' sets it inside the recluses. 'City dwellers' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Londoners live in the British capital, a city.

clue.text: Persistently question Unionist member after opening of Parliament

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Unionist MP grills ministers after Parliament opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only places U and MP after P.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to interrogate them repeatedly for information.

clue.text: Former dictator arrested by United Nations chap, but not questioned

indicators.note: the dictator is held inside, as one arrested is held by captors

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, standing for any chap
ex means former
Idi Amin was the Ugandan dictator

explanation.surface: A UN officer arrests an ex-tyrant but never interrogates him.
explanation.walkthrough: Idi Amin ruled Uganda in the 1970s. 'arrested by' sets the ex-dictator inside the United Nations chap; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexamined has never been looked into or queried.

clue.text: Spending freely to make tape of girl distorted

indicators.note: twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl's recording warped into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges TAPE OF GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate person is recklessly extravagant with money.

clue.text: Ship's one good worker getting trapped in sea water

indicators.note: the pieces end up enclosed inside the salt water

parts.note: brine is salty sea water
I is the Roman numeral one
the ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A ship's single good hand gets caught in the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting trapped in' puts I + G + ANT inside BRINE; the 's after Ship stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Form of Buddhism attracts old Greek philosopher

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism stressing meditation

explanation.surface: Zen draws in an ancient Greek thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracts' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno of Elea, famed for his paradoxes, was an ancient thinker from the Hellenic world.

clue.text: Unspecified amount of currency to encourage medical practitioner

parts.note: n stands for an unspecified number in maths
euros are the European currency
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A bit of money is offered to spur a doctor on.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the mathematician's symbol for an unknown amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain surgeon is a specialist doctor.

clue.text: To enlist in military detachment, give full particulars

parts.note: to go into the army is to enlist in it
a detail is a small group of soldiers given a special task

explanation.surface: Joining an army squad, someone explains everything thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: A detail is a small group of soldiers assigned a particular duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into detail is to explain something thoroughly, point by point.

clue.text: With money up front, composed score for Ionescu play

indicators.note: the money is placed at the front of the answer, above the rest in a down clue

parts.note: rhino is old British slang for money

indicators.note: arranged afresh, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cash in advance for writing music for an Ionesco drama.
explanation.walkthrough: RHINO is old British slang for money. 'composed' turns SCORE into CEROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoceros is Eugene Ionesco's absurdist play about townsfolk turning into the beasts.

clue.text: Here in the Deep South, stick on some make-up

parts.note: a bat is a stick used in games
taken as written
rouge is a red cosmetic for the cheeks

explanation.surface: Down south, someone applies a little make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Note 'stick' is BAT, not BATON, which would leave an extra ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Louisiana lies in the region of the US called the Deep South.

clue.text: Sound of school principal's voice is only partly grave

parts.note: a head is a headteacher; the possessive adds an S
tone is the quality of a voice

explanation.surface: The headteacher's tone is only somewhat stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' is not an adjective about the voice: it is the burial place, and the stone is just one part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravestone marks a burial plot, forming one part of the whole tomb.

clue.text: Start to make speech, having imbibed single drink

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so the drink goes into the speech word

parts.note: to orate is to deliver a speech
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A speaker downs a gin before beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having imbibed' signals a container: the speech-maker swallows the single drink. 'Start' at the front is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or arise.

clue.text: Heartless Rumpelstiltskin, finally repenting… thus?

indicators.note: the whole inner part of the long name is removed, leaving just its ends
the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale imp, robbed of his prize, ends up sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' strips the middle of the name to leave RU...IN; 'finally' adds G. Read as a whole, the clue describes the imp regretting his bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing means regretting, the very state of someone repenting.

clue.text: One fellow returns holding ring for woman

indicators.note: the reversed pieces hold the ring inside them
the two pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a man is a fellow
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A lone man comes back with a wedding ring for a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns I + MAN into NAMI, and 'holding' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, from the Book of Ruth.

clue.text: Demanding sister should be included in plan

indicators.note: the sister is placed within the word for plan

parts.note: an intent is a purpose or plan

explanation.surface: A bossy sibling insists on being part of the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' is the container signal; 'should be' is a link. 'Demanding' looks like a description of the sister but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistent means pressing, making firm demands.

clue.text: Having squashed snails, grocer waits on the doorstep?

indicators.note: crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who has trodden on snails lingers by the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squashed' rearranges SNAILS and GROCER. Waits are carol singers going door to door at Christmas, an old British word; the noun is disguised as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Waits is an old name for bands of Christmas street singers, who perform at front doors.

clue.text: To fall asleep before beginning of film is a mistake

indicators.note: the blunder comes ahead of the letter taken from the film

parts.note: a goof is a blunder

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Nodding off before the movie starts is an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' puts GOOF ahead of F.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off is to drop off into sleep.

clue.text: Run fast, rescuing maiden from seraglio

indicators.note: taking the maiden out of the harem removes her letter from it

parts.note: a seraglio is a harem
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A captive girl is freed from the harem and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored, abbreviated M. 'rescuing' removes M from HAREM.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to dash at speed, like the animal.

clue.text: Hide dog, perhaps, round rear of kennel

indicators.note: the pet goes round the letter taken from the kennel

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A dog conceals itself around the back of its kennel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts PET around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is an animal's skin or hide.

clue.text: Run away after decisive defeat

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
out means away, as in gone out

explanation.surface: Someone flees after a crushing loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run away' looks like the definition, but it supplies R and OUT; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is an overwhelming defeat.

clue.text: Nobles refuse to admit individual standing at gate, distressed

parts.note: to bar someone is to refuse them entry
one means a single individual

indicators.note: upset or knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aristocrats bar a lone visitor waiting anxiously at the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' turns GATE into TAGE; 'standing at' only places it beside ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The baronetage is the collective body of baronets, a hereditary titled rank.

clue.text: Instituted legal proceedings against pretentious type, it's said

indicators.note: the word for the poser is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a pseud is a pretentious poser

explanation.surface: Someone took a show-off to court, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: PSEUD is British slang for a pretentious person; the P is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To have taken someone to court is to have brought a lawsuit.

clue.text: Creature chewed finest lace

indicators.note: chewed up and mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some animal has nibbled the best lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges FINEST LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf insect is an animal camouflaged to look like foliage.
